CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zuid is a complete UUID implementation for R with two rings around it. The core is RFC 9562 in full: versions 1 to 8, nil and max, name-based and monotonic generation, every RFC text form. The first ring re-encodes the same bytes (Crockford base32, base36, base58, base62, base64url, Base62sort and Base64sort, any alphabet, Proquint, Niceware words). The second ring is the kindred formats: ULID, TypeID, UPID, SCRU128, SCRU64, KSUID, Snowflake and Sonyflake, XID, ObjectId, NanoID, Cuid2, Sqids and CID. Generators are named after their format (uuid(), ulid()), and one id_ vocabulary detects, parses, validates, reads fields and time, and converts across all of them.

No Imports and no vendored code. v0.1.0 has no interface with other zu* packages: Arrow interchange (zuarrow), integers (zuint), name-based UUIDs and CID generation (zucrypt) and exact instants (zutempo) come after it, as Suggests. It is not a hashing package, not a random number generator, not a database driver, and in v0.1.0 not a password generator.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0043. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design doc decides. The roadmap is .agents/roadmap.md; its “After 0.1.0” section lists what was deferred, and why.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11. All twelve roadmap stages (0 to 11) are merged, and v0.1.0 was submitted to CRAN on 2026-11-06 (CRAN-SUBMISSION); it is in the incoming queue. Every format above parses, validates and reads its fields. Not in v0.1.0, by the maintainer’s 2026-10-24 scope cut: name-based UUID versions 3 and 5, cid() generation, Cuid2 generation, id_integer(), id_time(class = "zutempo"), Sqids numbers of 2⁵³ or more, and Arrow and DuckDB interchange.

The design’s speed targets (§10) are a record, not a gate (D15). .agents/benchmarks.md holds the measurements; most targets are not met, and creating 10⁶ R strings alone takes about 680 ms on the benchmark machine.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #2 for v0.1.0; the CRAN-submission issue is #15. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none. The design names consumers that will call the R functions (zucbor, zumsgpack, qio, zujson, mdbx, dastash, zudedup, openlineage). A C API for them, inst/include/zuid.h, is a later version, not v0.1.0.

Commands

Maintainer tooling under tools/, run from the package root. None of what these need is a package dependency.

tools/gen-tables            # regenerate the Niceware and Sqids tables
tools/gen-tables --check    # verify only; exit 1 if a written file differs
tools/gen-fixtures          # encodings, UPID, SCRU128, SCRU64 oracles (Python)
node tools/gen-js-fixtures.mjs   # Sqids and CID oracles (JavaScript)
tools/gen-determinism       # rewrite tests/testthat/fixtures/determinism.txt
tools/run-benchmarks        # design §10 timings, as rows for benchmarks.md
tools/run-benchmarks baseline    # the uuid and ulid baselines only
  • tools/gen-tables needs R 4.5 or later (tools::sha256sum) and yaml. It writes R/sysdata.rda, src/zuid_tables.h and src/zuid_tables.c.
  • tools/gen-fixtures runs in a virtual environment holding exactly the Python versions pinned in tools/fixture-sources.yaml; its docstring has the pip install line. tools/gen-js-fixtures.mjs reads ZUID_NODE_MODULES; its header has the npm install line.
  • tools/gen-determinism regenerates zuid’s own output. Run it only for a change that is meant to alter generated values, and review the diff line by line.
  • tools/run-benchmarks needs bench, uuid and ulid.

Architecture

Five layers (design §4):

  1. Format descriptors, src/zuid_formats.c and src/zuid_formats.h. One static record per format. The R surface reaches every format through this table, so a new format is a new row and a new zuid_fmt_*.c, never a new entry point. Snowflake layouts and SCRU64 node sizes are descriptors built at run time from id_layout().
  2. Encodings, src/zuid_enc*.c. Codecs over bytes of any length. A UUID text form other than the hex ones is the 16-byte case of one of these.
  3. Formats, src/zuid_fmt_*.c, plus src/zuid_sqids.c and src/zuid_cid.c. Parse, validate and fields over the descriptor.
  4. Generators, src/zuid_gen.c. Pure functions of (n, time, random bytes, node) plus the monotonic state they are handed. src/zuid_entropy.c reads the clock and the operating system’s entropy source, for the R entry points only. Per-session monotonic state is one static struct, reset by zuid_c_reset_state.
  5. The R surface, R/ and the R-facing C files src/zuid_r*.c. Vectorisation happens in C: one loop per operation, filling parallel output vectors that R assembles once.

Everything except src/zuid_r*.c and src/zuid_init.c is plain C11 with no R headers. That split is what lets the fuzz workflow build the codecs without R (tools/fuzz/harness.c, -DZUID_STANDALONE).

src/zuid_tables.c (about 66,000 lines) and src/zuid_tables.h are generated by tools/gen-tables. Never edit them by hand.

The vctrs methods in R/zzz.R are registered only when vctrs is loaded, so zuid vectors combine in tibbles without vctrs being a dependency. vctrs double-dispatches on the first class, so each format registers its own pair.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No Imports. After 0.1.0 other zu* packages become Suggests, checked with requireNamespace(); a missing one raises zuid_dependency_error. In v0.1.0 no zu* package is referenced at all.
  • Entropy comes from the operating system, never R’s RNG (D5). An identifier must not change when a script calls set.seed(). Tests that need fixed output pass random in.
  • Generators are pure functions of (n, time, random, node) (D6). The clock and entropy are read once in the R entry point. Reading them inside a generator makes the fuzz target and the cross-platform byte-identity tests impossible. A call given both time and random leaves the session’s monotonic state alone.
  • 128 bits do not make a UUID (D3, D9). id_from_bytes() has no default format, and only uuid exports to Arrow as arrow.uuid; every other format uses zuid.<format>. A ULID arriving as arrow.uuid is the bug this prevents.
  • Detection never guesses (D10). An encoding or syntactic format needs a hint; ambiguity among structured formats is NA with candidates.
  • Inspection never raises on input. id_detect(), id_valid(), id_fields(), id_time() and id_parse(strict = FALSE) return NA.
  • The only place a CHARSXP is made from bytes is one function in src/zuid_r.c, so encoding and length rules live in one place.
  • The shared object exports R_init_zuid only. src/Makevars passes $(C_VISIBILITY) to hide every zuid_* symbol, and test-abi.R checks the installed object. Internal native symbols use the zuid_ prefix, and .Call entry points zuid_c_.
  • The codec files include no R headers. Adding one breaks the fuzz build, which compiles every src/*.c except the R-facing files.
  • No vendored code (D7). The Sqids blocklist and the Niceware word list are generated tables with source, date and SHA-256 in tools/fixture-sources.yaml, and their authors are listed as cph in DESCRIPTION and in inst/COPYRIGHTS.
  • TypeID’s fixtures stay out of the tarball. They are Apache-2.0, so .Rbuildignore excludes tests/testthat/fixtures/typeid, and the tests that read them skip on CRAN and when the files are absent.

Testing

The oracles are the thirteen of .agents/design.md §7: RFC 9562 Appendices A and B, TypeID’s valid.yml and invalid.yml, and the ULID, UPID, SCRU, KSUID, XID, Sqids, Proquint, Niceware and CID reference vectors, among others. They are stored under tests/testthat/fixtures/ at the commits and versions pinned in tools/fixture-sources.yaml, and written by the tools/gen-* scripts above.

fixtures/determinism.txt is zuid’s own output, not an oracle. It guards that every platform produces the same bytes; the oracle tests check that the bytes are right.

Helpers in tests/testthat/helper-*.R:

  • helper-abi.R: the symbol audit, after zucrypt’s. It is a helper so that testthat’s parallel workers see it too.
  • helper-class.R: three parsed UUIDs, the last missing.
  • helper-detect.R: every collision design §6.2 names, as a table of string, hint, layout, expected format and candidates.
  • helper-determinism.R: every generator and encoding on fixed inputs, as the lines of determinism.txt.
  • helper-enc.R: the Go and Python encoding oracle.
  • helper-formats.R: a small reader for TypeID’s YAML fixtures, since zuid has no YAML dependency.
  • helper-gen.R: local_fresh_state(), which resets the per-session generation state for a test and again after it, and hex_raw().
  • helper-uuid.R: the RFC 9562 test vectors.

Continuous integration

The package calls r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml, coverage.yml and cran-release.yml, fuzz.yml from fuzz.yaml, and from native-checks.yaml the sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers and cran-special workflows. The pkgdown site is built by a local pkgdown.yaml.

Deliberate deviations from .claude/shared/ci.md:

  • A push to main runs the full profile. The callers pass quick only for a pull request without full-ci, not profile: auto. Don’t wait on the full run a merge starts; a failure only it shows goes on an issue with the run link.
  • R-CMD-check.yaml adds Windows R-devel, CRAN’s r-devel-windows-x86_64 flavour, and the NOSUGGESTS and NOLD flavours, in the full profile only.
  • Fuzzing runs on every pull request: two minutes, and an hour nightly and under full-ci. The seed corpus is tools/fuzz/corpus, drawn from the oracle fixtures, and the dictionary is tools/fuzz/zuid.dict. Every broken round trip aborts, which libFuzzer reports as a crash.
